requirement.text: If an ETCS equipped train passes a level transition to a line fitted with more than one level, the onboard shall switch to the highest level, according to the priority given by trackside, for which it is equipped.

classification.rationale: The target requirement specifies onboard rail equipment behavior for the European Train Control System (ETCS), which is an embedded/safety-critical railway control system rather than a web, mobile, or AI system.

rounds.text_checked: If an ETCS equipped train passes a level transition to a line fitted with more than one level, the onboard shall switch to the highest level, according to the priority given by trackside, for which it is equipped.

test_strategy.rationale: Decision table testing applies because the level selection depends on multiple combined conditions: available trackside levels, trackside priority ordering, and onboard equipment capabilities. State-based testing applies because the requirement governs transitions between distinct ETCS operating levels as the train crosses a transition point. Equivalence partitioning applies to group onboard capability configurations and trackside priority lists into valid equipped versus non-equipped equivalence classes.

test_cases.title: Highest Priority Trackside Level Selection when Fully Equipped
test_cases.preconditions: Train onboard is configured and equipped for ETCS Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3. Train is operating in Level 1.
steps: Receive trackside level transition announcement offering Level 3 (Priority 1), Level 2 (Priority 2), and Level 1 (Priority 3).
test_cases.expected_result: The onboard unit evaluates available trackside levels against its equipment capabilities and switches to Level 3, as Level 3 is the highest priority trackside level for which the onboard is equipped.

test_cases.title: Fallback to Lower Priority Trackside Level when Not Equipped for Top Priority
test_cases.preconditions: Train onboard is equipped for ETCS Level 1 and NTC, but NOT equipped for Level 2 or Level 3. Train is currently operating in Level 1.
steps: Receive trackside level transition announcement offering Level 2 (Priority 1), Level 1 (Priority 2), and NTC (Priority 3).
test_cases.expected_result: The onboard unit skips Level 2 because it is not equipped for it, and switches to Level 1, which is the highest priority trackside level for which the train is equipped.

test_cases.title: State Transition across Level Boundary with Multi-Level Trackside Information
test_cases.preconditions: Train onboard is in 'Level 0' state and equipped for Level 1 and Level 2.
steps: Drive the train towards the level transition balise group.
Pass the balise group containing level transition data (Trackside Priority: Level 2 > Level 1).
Verify state transition trigger processing on crossing the transition point.
test_cases.expected_result: The onboard state transitions from 'Level 0' directly to 'Level 2' state upon passing the transition point.

test_cases.title: Equivalence Partitioning for Equipped vs Non-Equipped Multi-Level Selections
test_cases.preconditions: Train onboard is equipped for Level 2 and Level 0, but NOT Level 3.
steps: Configure trackside balise group to transmit multi-level transition order: Priority 1 = Level 3, Priority 2 = Level 2, Priority 3 = Level 0.
Pass the transition balise group with the train.
Observe selected ETCS level on the DMI and ETCS onboard unit.
test_cases.expected_result: The onboard unit partitions the trackside priorities into equipped {Level 2, Level 0} and non-equipped {Level 3} classes, selecting Level 2 as the highest priority equipped level.

final_text: If an ETCS equipped train passes a level transition to a line fitted with more than one level, the onboard shall switch to the highest level, according to the priority given by trackside, for which it is equipped.
